quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #16
										  					
  

40 Questions • Passing Score 32

questions.question: What does a "No passing zone" sign tell drivers?

options.text: Speed up a little.
It is not safe to pass.
Keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is not safe to pass.
questions.explanation: A "No passing zone" sign means you cannot pass other vehicles in that area. The road ahead has limited visibility, making it unsafe to pass.

questions.question: When bad weather or dark conditions require your lights on, which should you use?

options.text: Parking lights.
High beams.
Low beams.

questions.correctAnswerText: Low beams.
questions.explanation: Use low beam headlights in fog, snow, or rain. High beams reflect off water and mist, creating glare and making it harder to see.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, when can you proceed in the direction of the arrow?

options.text: After you come to a complete stop.
When the light changes.
When you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are in the correct lane and the intersection is clear.
questions.explanation: You can go with a green arrow if you are in the right lane and no pedestrians or vehicles are in the intersection. Always yield to anyone already in the intersection.

questions.question: When must you use your low beams?

options.text: On a lit street.
On a freeway.
In fog.

questions.correctAnswerText: In fog.
questions.explanation: Use low beams in fog, snow, rain, or mist. High beams reflect off these conditions and create glare. Some cars have fog lights that work with low beams.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Cars on the right go first.
You have the right-of-way.
Let other traffic pass before you go.

questions.correctAnswerText: Let other traffic pass before you go.
questions.explanation: This sign means yield. Slow down and let other vehicles and pedestrians cross in front of you. Stop if you need to.

questions.question: When passing another vehicle, you should:

options.text: Not expect the other driver to make room for you to return to your lane.
Assume the other driver will let you pass if you signal.
Assume the other driver will keep the same speed.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not expect the other driver to make room for you to return to your lane.
questions.explanation: Even with a turn signal, do not assume other drivers will give you space or right-of-way.

questions.question: What does this road sign mean?

options.text: Flagger ahead.
Turn left at the intersection.
Last turn before a toll road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Flagger ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs mark construction zones. This sign warns you a flagger is ahead. You must follow the flagger's directions.

questions.question: Which statement is true about drugs and driving?

options.text: Any prescription drug is safe to use if you don't feel drowsy.
Over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
Only illegal drugs can impair your driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Over-the-counter drugs can impair your driving.
questions.explanation: Legal drugs—both prescription and over-the-counter—can impair your driving. This includes drugs for colds, allergies, and anxiety. It is illegal to drive while impaired by any drug.

questions.question: Which statement is true about work zones?

options.text: Fines for violations are the same as regular traffic violations.
You must slow down for the cone zone.
Only slow down if you think workers are present.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must slow down for the cone zone.
questions.explanation: Slow down and be ready to stop in work zones. This keeps drivers, pedestrians, and workers safe.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: The road changes direction or gets narrower.
No right turn.
No passing zone.

questions.correctAnswerText: The road changes direction or gets narrower.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that the road is about to curve or become narrower. You may see several of these signs on sharp curves or before narrow bridges.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A stop sign is ahead.
Side road.
Railroad warning.

questions.correctAnswerText: A stop sign is ahead.
questions.explanation: This sign warns you that a stop sign is coming up.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: A steep hill is ahead.
Trucks are not allowed on the hill ahead.
A logging road is ahead.

questions.correctAnswerText: A steep hill is ahead.
questions.explanation: Yellow warning signs have black markings. This sign warns drivers about a steep hill coming up. Slow down and be ready to control your speed to protect your brakes.

questions.question: When driving on snow or ice, what should you do?

options.text: It is safe to use cruise control.
Change speed and direction slowly and carefully.
Drive the same way as in normal conditions.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change speed and direction slowly and carefully.
questions.explanation: On snow or ice, change speed and direction slowly. Do not use cruise control on snow or ice because your tires may lose grip and you could lose control of your vehicle.

questions.question: How can you avoid losing grip on wet roads?

options.text: Make sharp turns.
Brake hard.
Slow down.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down.
questions.explanation: Reduce your speed on wet roads to prevent hydroplaning. Keep your tires in good condition. If you feel your vehicle sliding, take your foot off the gas and do not brake. Keep the vehicle going straight and let it slow down on its own.

questions.question: At a red light with a green arrow, when can you go?

options.text: After you come to a complete stop.
When the main light turns green.
When you are in the correct lane and the road is clear.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you are in the correct lane and the road is clear.
questions.explanation: If you are in a lane with a green arrow, you can go in that direction when it is safe. This is true whether the arrow appears alone or with other lights.

questions.question: Where are a truck's blind spots?

options.text: Directly behind the truck.
On the left side of the cab.
On the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.

questions.correctAnswerText: On the left side of the cab and directly behind the truck.
questions.explanation: Trucks have large blind spots. The driver cannot see cars directly behind or to the left of the truck. If you cannot see the driver's face in their mirror, they cannot see you.

questions.question: If someone is tailgating you on a multilane highway, what should you do?

options.text: Speed up to match their speed.
Move right and let them pass.
Slow down to teach them a lesson.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move right and let them pass.
questions.explanation: If someone is following too closely on a multilane road, move to the right lane and let them pass. The left lane is for faster-moving vehicles to pass slower ones.

questions.question: When driving at night on a dark street, what should you do?

options.text: Drive slow enough to stop within your headlights' light.
Use high beams to see ahead better.
Keep your dashboard lights bright so others can see you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slow enough to stop within your headlights' light.
questions.explanation: Drive more slowly at night than during the day. Make sure you can stop your vehicle within the area lit by your headlights.

questions.question: What should you do at a school crossing sign?

options.text: Always stop, even if there is no stop sign.
Watch for children and be ready to stop.
Always honk your horn when you see children.

questions.correctAnswerText: Watch for children and be ready to stop.
questions.explanation: Pentagonal signs mean you are near a school. When you see these signs, stay alert and prepare to stop.

questions.question: What does a broken yellow line in the center of the road mean?

options.text: A construction zone is ahead.
No one can pass from either direction.
Anyone can pass from either direction.

questions.correctAnswerText: Anyone can pass from either direction.
questions.explanation: A broken yellow line means any driver may pass when there is no oncoming traffic.

questions.question: If you are following a school bus or tank truck, what should you do?

options.text: Pass them on the right.
Be ready to stop at all railroad crossings.
Expect them to drive faster than the speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be ready to stop at all railroad crossings.
questions.explanation: School buses and tank trucks must stop at all railroad crossings. Even if no train is coming, they have to stop. If you follow one of these vehicles, be ready to stop too.

questions.question: Your car breaks down on the highway. What should you do?

options.text: Stop in the right lane.
Move completely off the road if possible, with all four wheels off the pavement.
Stop where you are.

questions.correctAnswerText: Move completely off the road if possible, with all four wheels off the pavement.
questions.explanation: Get your car completely off the road when possible. All four wheels should be off the main road.

questions.question: When merging onto a freeway, how fast should you drive?

options.text: At about the same speed as traffic on the freeway.
5 to 10 mph slower than freeway traffic.
At the posted freeway speed limit.

questions.correctAnswerText: At about the same speed as traffic on the freeway.
questions.explanation: Merge onto the freeway at about the same speed as the traffic already on it.

questions.question: A car coming toward you has high beams on and you cannot see the road. What should you do?

options.text: Look toward the left edge of your lane.
Look toward the right edge of your lane.
Look straight ahead in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right edge of your lane.
questions.explanation: Do not look directly at the bright headlights. Instead, look toward the right edge of your lane. Watch the other car using your side vision.

questions.question: You hit a parked car and cannot find the owner. What must you do?

options.text: Call your insurance company when you get home.
Wait for the owner to return.
Leave a note with your name and address on the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave a note with your name and address on the car.
questions.explanation: You must leave a note on the car with your name, phone number, and address.

questions.question: When should you turn your wheels to the side instead of pointing them straight?

options.text: When waiting to turn left at a red light.
When parked on a hill or sloped driveway.
When parked on the side of a level road with no curb.

questions.correctAnswerText: When parked on a hill or sloped driveway.
questions.explanation: When parked on a hill or slope, turn your wheels away from the road. This keeps your car from rolling into traffic if the brakes fail. When waiting to turn left, keep wheels straight ahead.

questions.question: You want to turn left. Who has the right-of-way?

options.text: Other cars also turning left.
All other vehicles coming toward you.
Pedestrians on the sidewalk waiting to cross.

questions.correctAnswerText: All other vehicles coming toward you.
questions.explanation: You must let all other vehicles pass before you turn left.

questions.question: The light turns yellow as you approach an intersection. What should you do?

options.text: Slow down and drive through without being careful.
Speed up to cross before the light turns red.
Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stop before entering the intersection if you can do so safely.
questions.explanation: Yellow means the light will turn red soon. Stop if you can do so safely. If you cannot stop safely, cross carefully.

questions.question: When driving through a work zone, what should you do?

options.text: Follow the car in front of you closely.
Pass the car in front of you as soon as you can.
Keep a safe distance and do not tailgate.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep a safe distance and do not tailgate.
questions.explanation: In work zones, keep a safe distance from other vehicles, equipment, and workers. Do not tailgate.

questions.question: After you pass a car, when is it safe to return to your lane?

options.text: When the other driver signals you to return.
When you signal for three seconds.
When you can see the other car's headlights in your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you can see the other car's headlights in your rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: You have enough space to return to your lane when you can see both headlights of the passed car in your rearview mirror.

questions.question: When following a motorcycle, what should you do?

options.text: Stay farther back than usual.
Drive closer than normal.
Pass it right away.

questions.correctAnswerText: Stay farther back than usual.
questions.explanation: Motorcycles can turn and change lanes faster than other vehicles. Drivers of larger vehicles need extra space to react to sudden moves by motorcyclists.

questions.question: What should a driver watch?

options.text: Only straight ahead of the car.
Only the middle of the road.
The sides, ahead, and behind the car.

questions.correctAnswerText: The sides, ahead, and behind the car.
questions.explanation: Good drivers watch everything around their vehicle. This includes the sides, ahead, and behind to stay safe.

questions.question: How do you check your blind spot when changing lanes?

options.text: Use the inside rearview mirror.
Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
Use your side mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn your head and look over your shoulder.
questions.explanation: Mirrors cannot show all blind spots. Before changing lanes, always look over your shoulder to check these hidden areas.

questions.question: At a yield sign, what must you do?

options.text: Give the right-of-way to traffic that could cause a conflict.
Yield only to vehicles on your right.
Slow down but never stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Give the right-of-way to traffic that could cause a conflict.
questions.explanation: At a yield sign, give the right-of-way to traffic already in the lanes you want to enter. Be ready to stop, but you can go if there is no traffic.

questions.question: When turning left, who must you yield to?

options.text: Cars passing you.
Oncoming cars.
No one.

questions.correctAnswerText: Oncoming cars.
questions.explanation: You must yield to oncoming cars when turning left. You can only turn when it is safe and will not affect oncoming traffic.

questions.question: When roads are slippery after rain starts, what should you do?

options.text: Avoid fast turns and stops.
Test your tires' grip while going uphill.
Look less far ahead of your vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Avoid fast turns and stops.
questions.explanation: On wet, slippery roads, your tires have less grip. Drive slower and avoid sharp turns or sudden stops to prevent skidding.

questions.question: If there is a deep puddle ahead, what should you do?

options.text: Keep driving at the posted speed to get through the water.
Go around the puddle if you can.
Shift into neutral while driving through the water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Go around the puddle if you can.
questions.explanation: Avoid slippery areas like puddles, ice, wet leaves, and oil. The safest road surface is dry and solid.

questions.question: When backing up, what should you do?

options.text: Look through the rear window.
Press hard on the gas pedal.
Only use your rearview mirror.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look through the rear window.
questions.explanation: When backing up, look directly through the rear window. Do not rely only on mirrors, as they cannot show directly behind your vehicle. Back up slowly.

questions.question: When should you use your horn?

options.text: When another vehicle is in your way.
When it may help prevent a collision.
When another driver makes a mistake.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it may help prevent a collision.
questions.explanation: Only use your horn to avoid collisions. Do not use it to tell other drivers to go faster or move out of your way.

questions.question: Before making a turnabout, what should drivers do?

options.text: Honk to warn other drivers.
Make sure their car can be seen 500 feet ahead and behind.
Stop in the middle of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure their car can be seen 500 feet ahead and behind.
questions.explanation: A turnabout is a legal way to turn around. Before doing one, make sure your car is visible for at least 500 feet in both directions.
